title: Preparation and evaluation of brain-targeted thermosensitive in situ gel of geniposide
author: Yingting Wang
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.ks2cwge
materials: Gelation temperature of formulation: 1 Hydrogel (0.5 ml) was transferred to small (2 ml, 12 mm × 32 mm). 2 Vial was sealed and immersed into a thermostat controlled-electric water bath at an initial temperature of 20℃. 3 Temperature of the water bath was increased in increment of 0.5℃/min. 4 Mercury bulb of a thermometer with a minimum readable scale of 0.2℃ was placed at the same level with the hydrogel. 5 The meniscus of the hydrogel didn’t move when the vial was tilted 90 degree angle. The temperature was identified as the gelation temperature.

The gel strength: A sample of 50 g of hydrogel was put into a 100 ml graduated cylinder and gelled in a thermostatically controlled water bath at 37±0.5℃. A weight of 35 g was placed onto the gel. The gel strength was determined by the time in second as the weight penetrated 5 cm into the gel.

steps.title: Prepare the formulation
steps.instruction: Prepare the brain-targeted thermosensitive in situ gel using cold purified water and specific excipients.

substeps.instruction: Store purified water overnight at 4℃ in a refrigerator.
Slowly add the required amount of poloxamers into the required volume of cold purified water with continuous stirring.
Keep the upper hydrogel at 4℃ until a transparent hydrogel is obtained.
Disperse the required amount of hydroxypropyl methylcellulose, benzalkonium chloride, sodium chloride, geniposide, and borneol into the hydrogel with continuous stirring.
Adjust the final volume.

steps.title: Determine formulation pH
steps.instruction: Measure the pH of the formulation using a calibrated pH meter.

substeps.instruction: Calibrate the pH meter using solutions of pH 7.01 and pH 4.01.
Determine the pH value of the formulation.

steps.title: Measure mucoadhesive strength
steps.instruction: Evaluate the adhesive strength of the hydrogel using fresh goat nasal mucosa.

substeps.instruction: Prepare a section of fresh goat nasal mucosa and tie it to one side of two vials (2 cm diameter).
Place 50 mg of hydrogel on the nasal mucosa of one vial.
Attach the two nasal mucosa surfaces together for 2 min.
Pour water drop by drop into one container of the balance instrument until the two vials detach.
Weigh the minimal amount of water required for detachment.

steps.title: Perform in vitro release test
steps.instruction: Analyze the drug release from the hydrogel in a controlled temperature environment.

substeps.instruction: Transfer 5 g of cold hydrogel into a graduated test tube (1 cm diameter).
Place the tube in a water bath at 34±0.5℃ for 10 min.
Layer 2.5 ml of saline phosphate buffer (pH=6.4, 37±0.5℃) over the surface of the gel.
Remove the medium at one-hour intervals.
Clear the test tube, weigh it, and layer with fresh saline phosphate buffer (2.5 ml).

steps.title: Perform ex vivo drug permeation
steps.instruction: Measure the permeation of geniposide through goat nasal mucosa using a Franz diffusion cell.

substeps.instruction: Prepare a section of fresh goat nasal mucosa and fix it on a Franz diffusion cell with an effective permeation area of 2.8 cm².
Incubate for 30 min, then place 0.5 g of gel in the donor compartment.
Maintain the chamber temperature at 34±0.5℃.
Withdraw 6.5 ml of saline phosphate buffer (pH 6.4) from the receptor chamber at 30 min intervals and immediately replace with fresh buffer.
Determine the geniposide content of the sample using the HPLC method described below.

steps.title: Determine geniposide concentration via HPLC
steps.instruction: Quantify geniposide using high-performance liquid chromatography with the following parameters.

substeps.instruction: Use a C18 column (5 μm, 4.6 mm × 250 mm).
Set the mobile phase to acetonitrile: purified water (15: 85).
Set the detection wavelength to 238 nm.
Maintain the column temperature at 25℃.
Use an injection volume of 20 μl per sample.
